compatibility_evidence: 2026-10-07 security update, approved by the owner on 2026-10-07: source-map-js 1.2.2 (npm release 2026-09-30, BSD-3-Clause, integrity sha512-KGj/8Y43x35aZVDtt+J4mK1hoLGHULMYfSkODJNQjNDC3oW1PqPoxMwo0pLUsWM/UEGzON/NxeHywEfNXNP3Vw==, gitHead 0a1d334fd1e55a47df97fcd60a7915d46df3b08a, the commit of the upstream tag v1.2.2) replaces 1.2.1 in app/frontend/package-lock.json. 1.2.1 carries CVE-2026-93749 (GHSA-68fv-2mgg-jv7q, HIGH: event-loop denial of service through malformed indexed source-map section offsets; affected >=1.0.0 <1.2.2), fixed upstream by commit cf7658058ceeaa8619d5ae0ec90be6905209d016. source-map-js is a transitive development and build dependency only (vite 8.2.2 -> postcss 8.5.26 and @vitest/coverage-v8 4.1.11 -> magicast 0.5.4, both declaring ^1.2.1); it runs while the frontend is built and tested, and the frontend release image serves only the built static files. 1.2.2 is younger than 30 days and is recorded as a security exception. npm 11.19.1 `update source-map-js --package-lock-only` changed only the version, resolved and integrity lines of node_modules/source-map-js, and the resulting lock equals Dependabot #50's; package.json is unchanged, so the reviewed inventory (105 coordinates) and its digests stay as reviewed. The OSV query for npm source-map-js 1.2.2 on 2026-10-07 returned no advisory. Trivy 0.74.0 (vulnerability database of 2026-10-07): app/frontend/package-lock.json reports 1 HIGH finding before (source-map-js 1.2.1, CVE-2026-93749) and 0 findings at every severity after. The linux/amd64 frontend build stage (app/infra/Dockerfile.frontend.release --target build, connected mode, node:22.23.2-alpine3.23 base) drops from 27 to 26 HIGH or CRITICAL findings; the only finding removed is CVE-2026-93749. The 26 that remain predate this change and are outside it: OpenSSL 3.5.7-r0 of the pinned Node.js base image (CVE-2026-14456, 2 HIGH), packages bundled with npm 10.9.8 in that base image (1 CRITICAL, 13 HIGH) and the Go runtime inside the TypeScript 7.0.2 native compiler @typescript/typescript-linux-x64 (10 HIGH). Compatibility on 2026-10-07: npm ci --ignore-scripts installs source-map-js 1.2.2, and frontend lint, 144 tests and the production build pass on the host (Node.js 22.23.2). scripts/quality-gate.sh all passed on a separate Compose project whose frontend development image was built from the new lock and installs source-map-js 1.2.2 (backend lint, strict types, 726 unit and PostgreSQL 17.10 integration tests, database validation, OpenAPI contract, frontend lint, build, 144 tests and generated types, governance drift and Helm render). This is local evidence; it is not evidence of the GitHub checks, the image publication or the nonprod deployment.

2026-10-07 (kt-scaffold authority generation 50, factory main 36e46bc with PR #188): the owner accepts Python 3.12 and every later release regardless of known CPython advisories, with no patch-level security floor and no upper bound. app/backend/pyproject.toml declares requires-python >=3.12 with Black target py312 and mypy target 3.12 in place of >=3.14.7,<3.15, py314 and 3.14. The backend development, release and migration images stay on python:3.14-alpine3.23@sha256:218761489de417a6eb0808e264cbdd7043ec6659fe5a61898815e9848536541d (Python 3.14.7) and the three locks keep their Python 3.14 compile header. No package coordinate changes; the reviewed inventory stays at 105 coordinates. On macOS arm64 the hash-locked requirements.txt with requirements-dev.txt, and requirements-llm.txt on its own, install with --require-hashes --only-binary=:all: on CPython 3.12.15, 3.13.15 and 3.14.7 and pip check reports no broken requirement. PyPI publishes a CPython 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 wheel (or a pure-Python or abi3 wheel) at the locked version for musllinux x86_64/aarch64, macOS arm64 and Windows amd64 for each of the 95 coordinates of the three locks, pyodbc 5.3.0, grpcio 1.83.1 and ldap3 2.9.1 included, except uvloop 0.22.1, which publishes no Windows wheel for any series. With a Python 3.12 target, eight multi-type except clauses regain their parentheses and sixteen annotations that Python 3.12 would evaluate before the named type exists at run time are quoted again (tests/unit/test_readiness.py takes the factory's own fix); Ruff F821/F822 at py312 and a parse of every Python file at Python 3.12 syntax are clean. Backend Ruff, Black, isort and strict mypy pass on 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14, and the 726 backend unit and PostgreSQL 17.10 integration tests pass on each of the three series. The open-source licence Agent now names pyjwt==2.15.0. Evidence: docs/evidence/2026-10-07-python-3-12-plus-profile.md in factory source.

2026-10-02 security update, approved by the owner (kt-scaffold factory main 0db677c with PR #177; docs/evidence/2026-10-02-nginx-pcre2-security-update.md in factory source). Frontend: nginx:1.31.6-alpine-slim@sha256:f761b94f2cb9e8e05e2943d5f773609596113ef69b54e2433a996d109a8f78b7 (nginx 1.31.6, Alpine 3.24.2 OCI index, linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, published 2026-09-23) replaces nginx:alpine@sha256:4a73073bd557c65b759505da037898b61f1be6cbcc3c2c3aeac22d2a470c1752 (nginx 1.31.3, Alpine 3.24.1) in the frontend release image, the local Compose reverse proxy, the local-egress gate and the image workflow. Trivy 0.74.0 (vulnerability database of 2026-10-02) reports 18 HIGH findings for the previous base (OpenSSL 2, libuuid 7, libexpat 5, pcre2 4); the slim variant ships neither libexpat nor libuuid. No published official nginx Alpine image carries pcre2 10.49-r0 (CVE-2026-103111, HIGH, Alpine package published 2026-10-01), so app/infra/locks/nginx-alpine-packages.lock pins it (BSD-3-Clause) by exact version and SHA-256 for both architectures and app/infra/Dockerfile.frontend.release installs it after the digest check, with apk's own signature check and without consulting a repository. Backend: Alpine v3.23 replaced OpenSSL 3.5.8-r0 with 3.5.9-r0 on 2026-09-30 and its index no longer lists the locked 3.5.8-r0 packages (libssl3-3.5.8-r0.apk for x86_64 returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-02), so an uncached build of the backend development or release image stops. The Microsoft driver package declares a dependency on openssl, and the served openssl 3.5.9-r0 requires exactly libssl3=3.5.9-r0 and libcrypto3=3.5.9-r0, so app/infra/locks/backend-alpine-packages.lock moves the three packages to 3.5.9-r0 (Apache-2.0; .apk SHA-256 bytes observed from dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org on 2026-10-02, file sizes equal to the APKINDEX records). OpenSSL 3.5.9 (upstream release 2026-09-29) is a security patch release whose most severe fix is High; Alpine aports commit adcf4978 (main/openssl: security upgrade to 3.5.9) names the thirteen CVEs recorded in the exception. OSV queries for Alpine:v3.23 openssl 3.5.9-r0 and Alpine:v3.24 pcre2 10.49-r0 on 2026-10-02 returned no advisory. The three releases are younger than 30 days and are recorded as security exceptions; the reviewed inventory grows from 103 to 105 coordinates. Compatibility on 2026-10-02: the frontend and backend release images build without cache in connected mode for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 (pcre2 10.48-r0 -> 10.49-r0; libcrypto3 and libssl3 3.5.8-r0 -> 3.5.9-r0, openssl 3.5.9-r0). Trivy reports 0 findings at every severity for the frontend image on both architectures and 0 operating-system package findings for the backend image. The backend image still reports 1 CRITICAL and 9 HIGH Python package findings on both architectures, which this change does not address: PyJWT 2.13.0 (1 CRITICAL and 5 HIGH, fixed in 2.14.0; the kt-scaffold profile pin) and msgpack 1.1.2, setuptools 70.3.0 and urllib3 2.7.0 (4 HIGH), which the pinned Python base image itself carries. The frontend image served the application with HTTP 200 as user 101 on a read-only root file system with every capability dropped (nginx/1.31.6). On both backend images Python 3.14.7 links OpenSSL 3.5.9, unixODBC registers 'ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server', a pyodbc connection attempt reaches the driver (login timeout against a closed port) and pip check reports no broken requirement. tests/infra/local-egress.test.sh passed, including the gate configuration check on the new image. scripts/quality-gate.sh all passed on a separate Compose project with the development image rebuilt without cache from the new lock (backend lint, strict types, 726 unit and PostgreSQL integration tests, database validation, OpenAPI contract, frontend lint, build, 144 tests and generated types, governance drift and Helm render). Limits: the local Compose reverse proxy and the local-egress gate run the base image without a build and keep pcre2 10.48-r0; the proxy listens on the loopback address only and the gate publishes no port. Alpine does not keep superseded package versions, so a locked version stops downloading once its successor is published and the lock then has to move. This is a local build and scan; it is not evidence of the GitHub image publication or of the nonprod deployment.
